name: CDR ORINOQUIA
description:
The CDR ORINOQUÍA project, developed by Biofix Consultoría S.A.S BIC, is a large-scale afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) initiative designed to mitigate climate change by restoring degraded savannah ecosystems in the Orinoco region of Colombia. The project covers 8,441 hectares across seven private properties (Arizona, La Fortuna, La Carolina, San Andrés, Villa Claudia, Buenos Aires, and San Miguel) located in Puerto Gaitán, Meta.

The project employs a dual reforestation strategy:

Forest Plantations: Establishment of non-native species (Eucalyptus pellita and Pinus caribaea).

Natural Enrichment: Restoration of non-flood zones and flooded areas (gallery and moriche forests) using native species such as Cassia grandis, Hymenaea courbaril, Caraipa llanorum, Mauritia flexuosa, Euterpe precatoria, and Manilkara zapota.

To achieve its goals, the project operates a permanent nursery producing over three million seedlings annually. Implementation includes specialized machinery for site preparation, alongside GPS and drone technology for precise monitoring. This integrated approach aims to increase carbon sequestration and generate certified carbon credits while contributing to SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 8 (Decent Work), SDG 5 (Gender Equality) and SDG 15 (Life on Land). The project boundary encompasses all land parcels dedicated to these ARR activities as GHG sinks.

name: Brújula Verde
description:
Brújula Verde is a large-scale, 30,000-hectare reforestation and ecosystem restoration project in Vichada, Colombia, designed to deliver high-integrity nature-based carbon removals while supporting biodiversity and community development. The project focuses on establishing diverse, mixed-species forests through the planting of both fast-growing pioneer species and a wide range of native trees, 
ultimately transitioning toward predominantly native forest cover. This approach enhances soil recovery, 
improves water and nutrient cycles, and builds long-term landscape resilience. By combining phased 
planting and enrichment strategies, Brújula Verde strengthens ecosystem services, contributes to 
Colombia’s climate mitigation goals, and generates local employment and sustainable livelihood 
opportunities

name: Amazonia Nativa
description:
The Amazonia Nativa project seeks to create a new green cover with native species in a key region of Colombia through afforestation and reforestation efforts. The project will establish at least 7,500 hectares across 12 municipalities in the Southern Meta and Guaviare departments. The goal is to provide local stakeholders with sustainable land-use alternatives that offer equal or greater benefits compared to current practices. The project will adopt sustainable practices for managing planted native trees and açaí palms, such as Forest Sustainable Council. The project aims to pioneer the use of native species in large scale, creating timber products and açaí berries.

The project aims to increase the green forest cover in the Colombian Amazon and support the development of a sustainable wood value chain by planting native tree species on lands low-productivity degraded cattle ranching. 

Instead of a monocultural plantation, the project goes beyond common practice to produce sustainable wood by using a mix of native wood species, as well as açaí berries, removing on average 141,714 tCO2 annually. Selective low-impact logging will be employed instead of the clear-cutting harvesting.

name: BaumInvest Flor Saphira Reforestation Project El Capricho & La Catorce
description:
The "BaumInvest Flor Saphira Reforestation Project El Capricho & La Catorce" is the third Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) in Colombia incorporated into the Programme of Activities (PoA): BaumInvest Forest Landscape Restoration Programme (GS11707). The project focuses on ecological restoration of degraded cattle pastures in the Vichada department, Orinoquia region, municipality of Cumaribo, near the villages of El Capricho and La Catorce.

Key objectives include:

i) Climate change mitigation through long-term carbon sequestration via afforestation.
ii) Sustainable development and poverty alleviation by generating long-term employment in remote, economically underserved areas.
iii) Biodiversity conservation by preserving natural habitats and enhancing habitat connectivity.

This initiative integrates ecological, social, and economic dimensions to advance sustainable land use and restoration.

name: Sistema.bio Colombia Carbon Program: Waste management, clean energy and regenerative agriculture on family farms
description: Sistema.bio is a social enterprise that provides access to innovative biodigester technology, training and financing to address the challenges of poverty, food security, and climate change around the world. Sistema.bio manufactures and distributes high-quality, affordable biodigesters that enable farmers around the world to convert waste into energy and fertilizer. Sistema.bio works with farmers to ensure they become more sustainable, independent, and productive while mitigating the carbon emissions generated by agricultural activities. This program will provide a wide range of social, economic and environmental benefits for families and communities in Colombia through the installation of biodigesters. The program includes 7 sizes of biodigesters to adjust to the different types of farmers. The program will focus on smallholder dairy farmers, especially farmers who typically use woodfuel, charcoal or LPG for their energy needs both in the household and productive uses in the farm, and who currently do not manage the manure generated by their animals and have either solid or liquid storage practices for this. The program will be implemented Colombia.

name: BioGrow Energy
description:
BioGrow Energy is an emissions reduction project located in the municipality of Mapiripán, department of Meta, Colombia. The project aims to certify carbon credits and contribute to climate change mitigation through the recovery of methane in the wastewater treatment of the productive process of palm oil extraction from a 7,000-hectare plantation and the subsequent use of biogas for energy generation. The methane recovery and energy generation will be done through the construction and operation of a wastewater treatment plant with biodigesters, open lagoons and power generators with a capacity of 528 m3 of wastewater per day.

The project will generate CH4 and CO2 emissions reduction, considering the baseline scenario of the projects was a not well treated or overloaded wastewater management system and use of diesel for energy generation, where CH4 and CO2 emissions were produced.
